newsitem.title: UK: London funds worst hit by Olivetti fall-out - paper.
newsitem.headline: London funds worst hit by Olivetti fall-out - paper.

text.p: A group of large London-based shareholders face huge losses if a crisis at Italian computer giant Olivetti escalates, the Independent newspaper said in its Friday edition.

It said Olivetti's woes -- the loss-making group met Italian stock market watchdog Consob on Thursday in an attempt to clarify its financial accounts -- could prove most serious for a group of about 10 big London-based investment managers.
The paper said this group had "emerged collectively as the company's biggest shareholders following a 913 million stg rescue rights issue last December."

Between 30 and 40 percent of Olivetti shares are estimated to be held in London, with ING Barings Asset Management holding a stake of around six percent. This made it the largest shareholder after Carlo De Benedetti, it added.
De Benedetti, Olivetti's chairman, resigned suddenly on Tuesday as the group turned in another half-year loss.

On Wednesday Renzo Francesconi, a former Olivetti director general, resigned after only six weeks at the company, expressing misgivings about the way the group had presented its first half 1996 results.
